# MP161: Company-Scoped Schema Recognition

## Core Statement

**Schema yamls and their generated DDL artifacts SHALL be classified as either UNIVERSAL (used by all consuming companies) or COMPANY-SCOPED (used by exactly one company's data). The classification SHALL be visible from the file's directory path:**

- **Universal** → `_authoring/{core_schemas.yaml,platform_extensions/,_meta_schema.yaml,transformed_schemas.yaml}` and DDL output `_generated/{core,platforms}/`
- **Company-scoped** → `_authoring/companies/{COMPANY}/...` and DDL output `_generated/companies/{COMPANY}/platforms/{platform}/...`

The decision rule when classifying a new schema yaml: **"If a different company onboards tomorrow, would they reuse this exact shape?"**

- YES → Universal
- NO → Company-scoped

## Why This Rule Exists

GitHub issue #499 (2026-04-28): a user review of qef-product-master-redesign 9.5 acceptance outputs caught that `_generated/platforms/amz/` mixes 5 universal core datatype DDL files (sales/customers/orders/products/reviews) with 13 QEF-eyewear-specific DDL files (12 product_attributes_* + company_product_extension), with no architectural distinction visible from the file tree.

The user's observation:

> 「這邊不分公司行嗎？我覺得 bridge 絕對是要 company-specific」

The `bridges/{COMPANY}/{platform}/` layer was already correctly company-scoped, but the DDL layer that bridges populate was not. **The implicit assumption "all Layer 1 schemas are universal" broke when 13 datatypes shipped in 9.2/9.3 turned out to be QEF-eyewear-specific.**

This is the 5th implicit-to-explicit principle in Phase 9 (after MP159 #494 / MP160 #497 / DEV_R056 #498). The pattern:

```
implicit convention → AI mistake → user catches → elevation to normative principle
```

Each prior elevation paid for itself in 1-2 future failure-prevention rounds. Same cost asymmetry applies here: ~1 hour to author MP161, vs. recurring AI/human mistakes for similar future schema scoping decisions.

**Technical evidence the gap was real**: the validator (`validate_bridge_yaml.R`) emits an INFO when checking `product_attributes_rpl.bridge.yaml`:

> *"canonical field existence check skipped — datatype 'product_attributes_rpl' not found in core_schemas.yaml or platform_extensions/amz_extensions.yaml"*

The validator was looking only at universal-scope files. The lack of company scope **in the data model** concealed the gap from automated checks. MP161 closes this gap structurally.

## Architectural Definition

### What Universal owns

```
shared/global_scripts/01_db/raw_schema/_authoring/
  ├── core_schemas.yaml                  ← 6 universal datatypes
  ├── _meta_schema.yaml                  ← validator vocabulary
  ├── transformed_schemas.yaml           ← 2TR-layer schemas
  ├── platform_extensions/
  │   ├── amz_extensions.yaml
  │   ├── cbz_extensions.yaml
  │   ├── eby_extensions.yaml
  │   ├── shp_extensions.yaml
  │   └── official_website_extensions.yaml
  └── r_definitions/                     ← legacy R-defined schemas
```

DDL emission for universal schemas:

```
shared/global_scripts/01_db/raw_schema/_generated/
  ├── core/                              ← core-only DDL (no platform)
  └── platforms/{amz,cbz,...}/           ← per-platform DDL
```

These files are bound by MP102 v1.2 (Schema Contract, MP156 Tier-2). Edits trigger IC_P002 cross-company verification across all 5 consuming companies.

### What Company-Scoped owns

```
shared/global_scripts/01_db/raw_schema/_authoring/companies/
  └── {COMPANY}/                         ← per-company namespace
        ├── {schema}.yaml                ← company-specific schema yamls
        ├── {translation_map}.yaml       ← company-specific translations
        └── gen_*.R                      ← company-specific generators
```

DDL emission for company-scoped schemas:

```
shared/global_scripts/01_db/raw_schema/_generated/companies/
  └── {COMPANY}/platforms/{platform}/
        └── {datatype}.sql               ← per-(company × platform × datatype)
```

Currently only QEF_DESIGN has company-scoped schemas (12 per-PL attribute datatypes derived from eyewear product profile Gsheet exports). Other 4 companies (D_RACING, MAMBA, WISER, kitchenMAMA) currently have no company-scoped schemas — they use only universal schemas.

## Decision Rule

When authoring a new schema yaml, ask: **"If a different company onboards tomorrow, would they reuse this exact shape?"**

| If the answer is | Classification | Path |
|---|---|---|
| YES — generic concepts every consuming company has | Universal | `_authoring/{core_schemas.yaml \| platform_extensions/}` |
| NO — fields derive from one company's specific data | Company-scoped | `_authoring/companies/{COMPANY}/{schema}.yaml` |

Concrete examples:

| Schema | Classification | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| `sales` (order_id / customer_id / quantity / unit_price / amount / ...) | Universal | Every retail company has these concepts |
| `products` (thin master: product_id / brand / category / ...) | Universal | All catalogs need product identity |
| `reviews` (review_id / product_id / rating / review_text / ...) | Universal | All review datasets fit this shape |
| `company_product_extension` (sku / marketplace / cost / fee_fba / net_profit / ...) | Universal | Every Amazon seller has these accounting cols (Chinese source col names live in QEF's bridge yaml only) |
| `product_attributes_blb` (eyewear-domain cols: rating_clear_vision / dimension_lens_width / activity_blue_light_reading / ...) | Company-scoped | QEF eyewear-specific; D_RACING (racing accessories) wouldn't reuse |
| `product_attributes_sgf` (sunglasses fishing) | Company-scoped | Same — QEF eyewear-specific |

## Anti-Pattern Examples

### Anti-pattern A — Putting company-scoped schema at universal path

**Wrong**: author `product_attribute_schemas.yaml` (12 QEF eyewear datatypes) at `_authoring/product_attribute_schemas.yaml` because "Layer 1 schemas live at the top level". This conflates universal-Layer-1 with company-scoped-Layer-1.

**Right**: place at `_authoring/companies/QEF_DESIGN/product_attribute_schemas.yaml`. Reason: the 12 datatypes' fields (rating_clear_vision, dimension_lens_width, etc.) derive from QEF's specific eyewear product line catalog. A second consuming company would not have these exact datatypes.

### Anti-pattern B — Putting universal schema at company path

**Wrong**: author `company_product_extension` (SKU/marketplace/cost/fee/profit) at `_authoring/companies/QEF_DESIGN/financial_schema.yaml` because "currently only QEF has financial data". This violates D2's decision rule — the schema fields ARE generic, only the source data is currently QEF-only.

**Right**: keep `company_product_extension` in `_authoring/core_schemas.yaml` (universal). The Chinese source col names (商品成本-廠價, 頭程費, etc.) live in QEF's bridge yaml's `column_mapping`, not in the schema. Schema speaks English; bridges speak per-company source dialect. Future second-amz-seller onboarding inherits the same shape.

### Anti-pattern C — DDL output path divergence from schema location

**Wrong**: schema lives at `_authoring/companies/QEF_DESIGN/product_attribute_schemas.yaml`, but `_build.R` emits DDL to `_generated/platforms/amz/product_attributes_blb.sql` (universal location). The output path lies about the scope.

**Right**: company-scoped schemas emit DDL to `_generated/companies/QEF_DESIGN/platforms/amz/product_attributes_blb.sql`. The path mirrors the source's scope.

### Anti-pattern D — Implicit company-scope without `companies/` prefix

**Wrong**: author `_authoring/QEF_DESIGN/...` directly at `_authoring/` top-level (no `companies/` prefix). This mixes scope-tagged with universal-tagged at the same level — the same readability problem MP161 was created to fix.

**Right**: always use `_authoring/companies/{COMPANY}/...`. The `companies/` prefix groups company-scoped work cleanly.

## Boundary Cases

### Promotion: company-scoped → universal

When does a schema graduate from company-scoped to universal?

- A second consuming company adopts the same schema shape (or close enough that bridge-level translation suffices)
- The schema's design has been stable across 2+ companies' use
- IC_P002 cross-company verification confirms the schema is appropriate for all 5 consuming companies

Process:

1. File a spectra change documenting the promotion
2. Run IC_P002 cross-company verification
3. `git mv _authoring/companies/{ORIGINAL}/{schema}.yaml` → `_authoring/{schema}.yaml`
4. Update `_build.R` to discover from new location
5. Update bridge yamls' `schema_yaml_path:` references in all consuming companies' bridge directories
6. Commit message includes `Verified:` trailer naming all 5 companies

### Demotion: universal → company-scoped

When does a schema get demoted from universal to company-scoped?

- The schema turns out to only be used by one company despite living at universal location
- Another company is unlikely to reuse the exact shape (different domain, different source data structure)

Process:

1. File a spectra change documenting the demotion
2. Identify the actual consuming company
3. `git mv _authoring/{schema}.yaml` → `_authoring/companies/{COMPANY}/{schema}.yaml`
4. Update `_build.R` and bridge references
5. IC_P002 cross-co verification confirms no other company actually depends on the schema

Demotions are rarer than promotions but possible. The `company_product_extension` decision (D4 of this principle's design) is a near-miss demotion candidate that we kept universal — review and possibly demote if 6 months pass and no second amz-seller adopts it.

## Files Bound

| File | Status under MP161 |
|---|---|
| `shared/global_scripts/01_db/raw_schema/_authoring/core_schemas.yaml` | Universal Layer 1 — bound by MP102 + MP156 |
| `shared/global_scripts/01_db/raw_schema/_authoring/platform_extensions/*.yaml` | Universal Layer 1 (per-platform) |
| `shared/global_scripts/01_db/raw_schema/_authoring/companies/*/*.yaml` | Company-scoped Layer 1 |
| `shared/global_scripts/01_db/raw_schema/_build.R` | DDL codegen — emits to scope-correct output paths |
| `shared/global_scripts/00_principles/.claude/skills/glue-bridge/scripts/validate_bridge_yaml.R` | Validator — schema-aware check looks in companies dir |
| `shared/global_scripts/00_principles/.claude/rules/01-always.md` | Layer 3 quick-reference |
| `shared/global_scripts/00_principles/.claude/rules/02-coding.md` | Layer 3 full coding-time section |

## Change Discipline

### Adding a new universal schema

A change adding a universal schema (or universal datatype within `core_schemas.yaml`) SHALL:

1. Pass the decision rule's "next-company-reuse test"
2. IC_P002 cross-company verification (all 5 consuming companies SHALL be able to use the schema)
3. DOC_R009 three-layer sync if it adds normative semantics
4. `_build.R` emits DDL to `_generated/{core,platforms}/`

### Adding a new company-scoped schema

A change adding a company-scoped schema SHALL:

1. Place files at `_authoring/companies/{COMPANY}/`
2. Generators (if any) co-locate at the same directory
3. `_build.R` emits DDL to `_generated/companies/{COMPANY}/platforms/{platform}/`
4. IC_P002 verification scope is reduced — only the owning company's existing workflows need verification, but the change SHOULD still note the scope reduction explicitly in the commit message
5. If the schema later promotes to universal, the promotion is a separate spectra change (per Boundary Cases above)

### Modifying an existing classification

Promotion (company-scoped → universal) or demotion (universal → company-scoped) requires its own spectra change with explicit scope-change documentation. Do NOT silently move files between scopes; that breaks downstream bridge yaml references and reviewer expectations.

## Enforcement

### Code-level (mechanical)

`_build.R` discovers schemas at three locations and emits DDL accordingly:

- `_authoring/core_schemas.yaml` → `_generated/core/{datatype}.sql` + `_generated/platforms/{platform}/{datatype}.sql`
- `_authoring/platform_extensions/{platform}_extensions.yaml` → augments per-platform output
- `_authoring/companies/{COMPANY}/*.yaml` → `_generated/companies/{COMPANY}/platforms/{platform}/{datatype}.sql`

A misplaced schema (e.g., company-scoped content at top-level) emits DDL to the wrong path. The "byte-identical re-run" reproducibility check catches inconsistency over time.

### Validator-level (mechanical)

`validate_bridge_yaml.R`'s schema-aware check resolves the bridge's `prerawdata_source.company` and looks under `_authoring/companies/{COMPANY}/*.yaml` for the canonical-target datatype, in addition to `core_schemas.yaml` and `platform_extensions/{platform}_extensions.yaml`. A bridge referencing a datatype that doesn't exist in EITHER location = CRITICAL.

### Process-level (review discipline)

Pull requests / spectra changes adding new schemas SHALL state the classification (universal vs company-scoped) explicitly in the commit message. The decision rule provides a concrete test the reviewer can apply.

## Exemptions

The following are NOT MP161 violations:

- **`company_product_extension` staying universal in `core_schemas.yaml`** even though only QEF currently uses it. Per D4 of this principle's design: schema fields are generic accounting concepts; Chinese source col names live in QEF's bridge yaml only. Other amz-seller companies onboarding inherit the same shape. Reversibility: if 6 months pass and no second amz-seller adopts it, demotion via spectra change is bounded-cost.
- **Existing `bridges/{COMPANY}/{platform}/` layout** without `companies/` prefix. The bridges layer is already correctly company-scoped at a different directory; migrating to `companies/{COMPANY}/bridges/{platform}/` is churn for no architectural gain. Out of MP161's enforcement scope.
- **`r_definitions/` directory** (legacy R-defined schemas pre-yaml authoring). Currently universal-scoped; MP161 doesn't retroactively classify legacy code. Future R-definition additions SHALL follow MP161 if/when the codebase migrates fully to yaml authoring.
- **Generated artifacts at `99_archived/`**. Archived content is exempt from current normative rules per MP030 (Archive Immutability).
